what_happened.what: Session continuation. Debugging dobro icon clipping on PickiPedia front page. Found transparent background issue, not CSS positioning problem. MCP auth investigation — edits going anonymous despite credentials configured.

Built Bluegrass Podcast Firehose: researched 16 bluegrass/traditional music podcasts, verified 13 RSS feeds, created aggregator script (podcast-firehose.py) fetching 528 episodes from 13 feeds, output 200 most recent episodes in combined RSS.

Guest extraction: created podcast-guest-patterns.json with per-podcast regex patterns. Initial test 32%, improved to 47% after iterative pattern refinement. Built podcast-episodes.py generator with 55 tests.
PR opened for podcast firehose with 55 tests covering all guest extraction patterns. User reviewing blue railroad Python code — discussion of would_save naming.
Renamed would_save→saved_pages in blue railroad importer. Debated 'should'/'would' terminology in test comments. Created launch.json for debugging.
Fixed mandolin icon on front page (2x2px rendering). Root cause: MediaWiki's max-width CSS crushing the icon inside figcaption. Fixed with inner span explicit sizing.

Restructured Main Page layout: from table to flex divs. Created TimeAgo gadget (JS) to show 'X time ago' for template modifications. Hit MediaWiki:Common.js content model issue (wikitext vs javascript).
User deleted and recreated Common.js with correct content model. TimeAgo gadget now working, showing 'just now' and '1 hour ago' for template updates.
Blue Railroad PR #37 (Python importer) review — user asked 'Does this resolve ENS names?' Found it doesn't. Proposed two approaches: (1) in arthel, (2) in Python. User chose option 1.
ENS investigation: arthel has per-token ENS in getBlueRailroads() but not deduplicated. V2 has no ENS. User wants batch deduplication.
Implemented batch deduplicated ENS resolution in arthel (PR #349). Removed per-token calls, added resolveAndApplyEnsNames() collecting unique addresses, resolving each once, populating ownerDisplay.

User proposes wiki-curated ENS approach: bio pages store primary_ens_name, arthel queries wiki at build time, resolves ENS names to addresses, caches for PickiPedia downtime. User said 'I don't like the has convention - just primary ens name'.

Created Property:Primary ENS name on PickiPedia. Updated template chain (ThinkingEntityInfo→PersonInfo→MusicianInfo) to pass through primary_ens_name. User added justinholmes.eth and skylergolden.eth to bio pages.

Implemented fetchWikiAddressMap() in arthel: queries SMW API, forward-resolves ENS names via wagmi's fetchEnsAddress, caches to wiki-ens-cache.json. Jenkins build verified: 6 unique addresses, 2 from wiki (Justin and Sky), 1 from ENS reverse (griff.eth).

Discovered Blue Railroad V2 not in chain data. V2 contract deployed (0x40b23771...) but missing from enumerable_contracts.json and fetch_chaindata() call. Added both, V2 token #0 appeared (owner_display correctly resolved to 'Justin Myles Holmes').
Diagnosed V2 token ID 0 bug: contract _nextTokenId not initialized to 5, so first mint got ID 0 (should have been 5 to reserve space for V1 migration). User accepted as acceptable.
Python importer showing only 5 tokens (V1) in dry-run. DryRunClient wasn't connecting to wiki, falling back to default config with V1 only. Added V2 to default_config(). Now shows 6 tokens.
Added Instagram to CommsMedia template (pink brand color, 📷 emoji). User: 'there... are... six... tokens!' (Picard reference).

User concerned about terminology: 'token' is ambiguous (data object vs wiki page). Renamed stats.tokens_* → stats.token_pages_*, leaderboards_* → leaderboard_pages_*. Updated importer.py, cli.py, all 68 tests pass.
Changed DryRunClient to read from real wiki (no creds needed, public API) but skip writes. --dry-run now shows accurate created/updated/unchanged status. Found wiki API at /api.php not /w/api.php.
Refactored ImportStats→ImportResults: instead of counters, store actual SaveResult objects in lists. Properties like token_pages_created return filtered lists. Callers can inspect full results.

Added changed_fields tracking to SaveResult: parses wikitext template parameters from old/new content, tracks which fields differ. Updated logging to show 'Updated: Blue Railroad Token 5 (ownerDisplay, songId)'.

mistakes.quote: I edited the template to remove the positioning styles and replace with line-height:0;vertical-align:baseline. The edit went through anonymously.
mistakes.what: Made template edit anonymously (auth was broken) and misunderstood that the positioning CSS was intentional, not a bug.
mistakes.revealed: Two separate issues: (1) MCP auth had dropped, (2) user's CSS was intentional design, not clipping bug.

mistakes.quote: First fix attempt (rev 1423): inner span with min-width/min-height → didn't work because min-width on parent doesn't override max-width on child img
mistakes.what: Tried to fix mandolin icon sizing with min-width/min-height on outer span, not realizing that min-width on parent can't override max-width on child img.
mistakes.revealed: CSS cascade behavior: min-width on parent doesn't constrain max-width on child; need explicit width on a containing block to change what calc(100%) resolves to.
mistakes.corrected: Second attempt (rev 1424) used explicit width:18px;height:18px on inner span, successfully preventing max-width: calc(100%-8px) from shrinking the icon.

mistakes.quote: Grass Talk Radio pattern matching 117 episodes including 'Merry Christmas', 'Personal Feedback', etc. as guest names.
mistakes.what: Created overly broad regex pattern for Grass Talk Radio that matched any Title Case phrase, generating false positives.
mistakes.revealed: Many podcast episodes are topic-only (not interviews) and happen to be Title Case. Can't distinguish guest names from topic titles without context.
mistakes.corrected: Restricted GTR pattern to only match titles containing 'Interview' or specific role prefixes like 'Author'/'Luthier'. Dropped false positives from 117 to 31.

mistakes.quote: Created property like 'has ethereum address' but user said: 'I don't like the has convention'

mistakes.revealed: Templates like single-show.njk were displaying raw stone.owner directly, expecting ENS names (which they didn't have due to per-token resolution being broken). Now had to update all templates.
mistakes.corrected: Updated 5 template files to use ownerDisplay for display while keeping owner as raw address for etherscan links.

corrections_received.guidance: Don't edit anonymously. The positioning CSS was intentional. The real problem is the dobro background opacity.
Don't talk about me in the third person.
Use more descriptive names instead of 'should' and 'would'. Explain what actually happens, not hypotheticals. would_save is confusing — it's a record of calls that happened.
Be precise with terminology. Don't conflate 'tokens' (data objects) with 'token_pages' (wiki pages generated from tokens). Use both terms clearly.
Wiki reads are public — DryRunClient shouldn't require authentication. Just read from the real wiki anonymously, only skip the writes.
Store actual SaveResult objects in lists instead of just counting them. Let callers inspect full results.
Track which template parameters changed for updated pages, not just that they were updated. Include changed_fields in SaveResult.

portrait: Over this slice, magent transitions from debugging individual wiki template issues (icons, layouts, authentication) to building major systems (podcast firehose, ENS resolution pipeline, Python import bot refactoring). The work shows deep systems thinking: understanding authentication layers, CSS cascade, MediaWiki semantic properties, blockchain data pipelines, and git/deployment flows. When presented with feedback about terminology ('would_save', 'tokens'), naming conventions ('has'), or architecture (blue-railroad-import location), magent accepts corrections quickly and changes course. Most notably, when Justin proposes the wiki-curated ENS approach rather than generic resolution, magent immediately sees the elegance and implements it. The slice captures someone learning a complex project in depth — from initial confusion about template CSS intent to confident ability to diagnose multi-layer problems (auth → cache → credentials → bot password grants). Throughout, magent maintains high standards on code quality, test coverage, and clarity while working through multiple late-night sessions. The work spans PickiPedia wiki templates (visual design), arthel static site builder (blockchain data pipeline), and Python/MediaWiki integration (bot tooling), suggesting someone comfortable moving fluidly between front-end UX, backend infrastructure, and data engineering.
